findings.title: [P1] Parse `cached.value`, not the `{ value, stale }` wrapper
findings.body: `Cache.get` now returns `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null`, but after the `cached === null` guard, `src/profile.ts` still calls `JSON.parse(cached)` on the wrapper object. `JSON.parse` requires a `string` — this is a TypeScript type error, and if executed at runtime every cache hit stringifies the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws a `SyntaxError`, breaking the normal steady-state path (any second load of the same profile). Fix: `return JSON.parse(cached.value);`. Not P0 only because the miss path still works and compile setup is not visible in this fixture.

findings.title: [P3] Confirm serving `stale: true` entries as fresh is intended
findings.body: The diff deliberately surfaces a `stale` flag, but the updated hit path in `loadProfile` treats `{ value, stale: true }` identically to fresh data — no revalidation or expiry handling anywhere in the change. Serving stale-while-revalidate may be exactly the intent (the PR body says "preserving existing contracts", and the store may refresh internally), so this is a confirm-intended observation rather than a defect.

findings.title: [P3] Empty-string cache payloads now throw instead of falling back to the API
findings.body: Behavioral edge case introduced by the diff: previously a falsy cached value (`""`) fell through to `api.loadProfile(id)`; now `{ value: "", stale: false }` is non-null, takes the hit path, and `JSON.parse("")` throws. Realistic impact is low for this caller (`profile:${id}` entries are non-empty JSON serializations), but worth documenting or guarding if the empty-string fallback was load-bearing.

findings.title: [P3] Add cache-hit coverage for the new return shape
findings.body: No test exercises the changed non-null `Cache.get` contract or the profile cache-hit path. A simple cache-hit test would have caught the P1 above (`JSON.parse` receiving the envelope); it would also pin down the `stale` and empty-payload semantics this diff leaves implicit.
